gate_proposals.name: Oracle Freshness Gate
gate_proposals.description: Skip entry if last oracle update > 30min stale. Requires oracle timestamp from HL API. HL API currently does not expose oracle timestamp directly — would need to track timestamp delta between consecutive API polls.
gate_proposals.estimated_trade_impact: -2% to -5% trade days (conservative estimate for HL downtime events)
gate_proposals.feasibility: PARTIAL — HL API does not expose oracle_timestamp directly; proxy: detect if markPx unchanged for N consecutive polls

gate_proposals.name: Mark vs Oracle Deviation Gate
gate_proposals.description: Skip entry if |markPx - oraclePx| / oraclePx > 1%. Sanity check for oracle divergence. Current live data: PAXG dev=0.05%, SPX dev=0.14% — well within gate.
gate_proposals.estimated_trade_impact: -1% to -3% (would have triggered 0 days in 30d snapshot)
gate_proposals.feasibility: HIGH — oraclePx available via metaAndAssetCtxs endpoint

gate_proposals.name: Floor-Pinned FR Stale Detection
gate_proposals.description: Skip SPX entry if FR == 0.0000125 (HL floor) for >= 7 consecutive days. Distinguishes genuine low-carry from oracle floor-clamping. Trade-off: floor FR is technically valid carry (~11% annualized) — so blocking it may reduce expected return.
gate_proposals.implementation: if all(abs(fr - 1.25e-5) < 1e-10 for fr in spx_fr.tail(7)): skip_spx()
gate_proposals.estimated_trade_impact: -8% to -12% trade days (23% of SPX days are floor-pinned)
gate_proposals.estimated_sharpe_impact: -0.5 to -1.5 (significant — floor FR is real carry, not zero)
gate_proposals.feasibility: HIGH — computed from existing parquet data
gate_proposals.priority: LOW — floor FR is genuine carry, not oracle failure

G9_mark_oracle_dev.rationale: G9 is feasible (oraclePx available live), cheap to implement, current deviations minimal (PAXG 0.05%, SPX 0.14%). K370 patch: add G9 check in k302a_satellite_fetch.py before logging trade.

G8_oracle_freshness.rationale: HL API does not expose oracle_timestamp directly. Proxy detection (unchanged markPx for N polls) is imperfect. Current live snapshot shows normal deviation — no active staleness event. K371: Add proxy staleness detection (track markPx delta across hourly fetches).

G10_floor_fr_stale.rationale: Floor-pinned FR (0.0000125/hr = ~11% ann) is genuine carry, not zero. Blocking it would reduce expected return with no safety benefit. April 2026 10-day PAXG episode occurred during tariff shock — oracle functioning normally (1% cap rate-limited repricing). Sharpe simulation shows stale-FR scenarios do NOT degrade performance.

regulatory_notes.r12_16_cftc_context: R12-16 CFTC scrutiny targets HL HIP-3 overall. Oracle reliability is a likely focus. K297' uses 504d+ historical data; single bad oracle day has immaterial impact.
regulatory_notes.hl_oracle_transparency: HL HIP-3 oracle mechanism is public (deployer-defined, protocol-level). oraclePx exposed via metaAndAssetCtxs API — auditable in real-time. 1% per-update cap rate-limits manipulation but also rate-limits legitimate price jumps. This is a known design trade-off documented in HIP-3 spec.
regulatory_notes.k297_defense: K297' uses 504d historical FR data as backtest basis + 5d trend filter. Resilient to single bad oracle day. Prolonged failure (>14 days) would degrade Sharpe by ~1-2 points (simulation: negligible). SPX filter blocks negative-FR days; zero-FR days reduce exposure safely. Stale floor-pinned FR (0.0000125) passes filter but represents genuine carry.
regulatory_notes.main_risk: Primary oracle risk for K297': PAXG oracle failure during gold market dislocation (e.g., April 2026 tariff shock). 10-day floor episode observed Apr 2026. PAXG is always-on — no trend filter. G9 gate (mark vs oracle < 1%) mitigates manipulation risk; G8 freshness gate would add safety but requires HL timestamp API.
